articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Native Multimodal Reasoning and Extended Context
articles.summary: OpenAI officially released GPT-5, featuring deeply integrated multimodal reasoning across text, image, audio, and video inputs with a context window exceeding 1 million tokens. The model demonstrates significant improvements in long-horizon planning, mathematical proof generation, and agentic tool use, narrowing the gap on several AGI benchmarks. Enterprise API access includes new structured-output guarantees and fine-tuning capabilities for domain-specific deployments.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Scientific Reasoning Benchmarks
articles.summary: DeepMind unveiled Gemini Ultra 2, which sets new records on GPQA-Diamond, MATH-500, and a newly introduced multi-step scientific discovery benchmark. The model integrates a verifier-based reinforcement learning pipeline that substantially reduces hallucination rates in chemistry and biology domains. Google is rolling the model into its research tools suite, targeting pharmaceutical and materials science applications.

articles.title: Figure Robotics Begins Commercial Deployment of Figure 03 Humanoid in BMW Factories
articles.summary: Figure Robotics announced that its third-generation humanoid robot, Figure 03, has entered commercial deployment at two BMW manufacturing plants in South Carolina. The robots handle parts kitting, inspection, and light assembly tasks alongside human workers, leveraging onboard vision-language models for real-time task adaptation. Figure reports a 40% improvement in manipulation dexterity over its predecessor, with plans to scale to additional OEM partners by Q4 2026.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Demonstrates Autonomous Warehouse Operations in Live Demo
articles.summary: Tesla showcased its Optimus Gen 3 humanoid performing end-to-end warehouse logistics tasks including unloading, sorting, and shelving packages without human intervention for sustained 8-hour shifts. The demo highlighted improved balance recovery, fine-grained hand manipulation, and a new sim-to-real transfer pipeline that dramatically cuts deployment training time. Tesla confirmed limited commercial availability to select logistics partners beginning late 2026.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude Tool-Use Agents with Persistent Memory and Sandboxed Execution
articles.summary: Anthropic released a major update to its Claude platform enabling autonomous multi-step tool-use agents with persistent cross-session memory and sandboxed code execution environments. The system allows developers to deploy agents that can browse the web, write and run code, manage files, and maintain long-term project context within defined safety guardrails. Early adopters report significant productivity gains in software engineering and data analysis workflows.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm Gate-All-Around Process Node
articles.summary: TSMC announced the start of volume production on its A14 (1.4nm-class) process using gate-all-around nanosheet transistors at its Kaohsiung fab. The node delivers an 18% speed improvement and 30% power reduction over N2, with initial production allocated to Apple and NVIDIA for next-generation mobile and AI accelerator chips. This milestone reinforces TSMC's roadmap dominance and has implications for the power efficiency of future AI training clusters.

articles.title: Microsoft and Quantinuum Demonstrate Fault-Tolerant Logical Qubit Operations Below Error Threshold
articles.summary: Microsoft and Quantinuum jointly announced achieving below-threshold error rates on logical qubit operations using Quantinuum's latest trapped-ion system combined with Microsoft's qubit virtualization layer. The team executed over 100,000 consecutive logical CNOT gates with an error rate of 10⁻⁸, a critical milestone for practical quantum error correction. The result puts near-term quantum advantage for certain optimization and cryptographic problems within a plausible 3-5 year horizon.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics and Hyundai Unveil Next-Gen Atlas Platform with LLM-Driven Task Planning
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics, under Hyundai's robotics division, revealed an updated electric Atlas humanoid that integrates a large language model-based task planner for interpreting natural language instructions in unstructured environments. The system combines real-time 3D scene understanding with dynamic motion planning, allowing the robot to autonomously navigate construction sites and perform inspection routines. Field trials are underway with three major construction firms in South Korea and the United States.
